'''Bidyut Baran Chaudhuri''' ('''B. B. Chauduri''') is a senior [[computer scientist]] and an emeritus professor of [[Techno India University]] in [[West Bengal]], India. He is also adjuncted to [[Indian Statistical Institute]], where he was a professor for about three decades. He was the founding Head of Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Unit (which was established in 1994) of [[Indian Statistical Institute|ISI]]. Moreover, he was a J.C. Bose Fellow and [[Indian National Academy of Engineering]]<ref name=inae1>{{cite web|title=INAE Expert Pool|url=http://expert.inae.in/index.php/bidyut-baran-chawdhuri|publisher=INAE|accessdate=20 November 2018|archive-date=20 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120135813/http://expert.inae.in/index.php/bidyut-baran-chawdhuri|url-status=dead}}</ref> Distinguished Professor at [[Indian Statistical Institute|ISI]].

He was the vice-president of the Society for Natural Language Technology Research (SNLTR).<ref>{{cite web|title=Society for Natural Language Technology Research|url=http://www.nltr.org/|publisher=NLTR|accessdate=20 November 2018}}</ref>

His primary research contributes to the fields of computer vision, image processing and pattern recognition.<ref name=ieee2>{{cite web|title=IEEE Life Fellow Dictionary|publisher=IEEE|url=https://services27.ieee.org/fellowsdirectory/getdetailprofile.html?custNum=wuV%2FRGDgNqLkDSNuwOHoig%3D%3D&bccaptions=Chronological&bclocations=%2Ffellowsdirectory%2FmenuCHRONOLOGICAL.html%3FbeginYr%3D2001%26endYr%3D2001|accessdate=20 November 2018}}</ref> He is a pioneer of "[[Languages of India|Indian language]] script [[Optical Character Recognition|OCR]]".<ref name=ieee2/>

==Education==
Chaudhuri received his BSc (Hons.), BTech and MTech degrees from [[University of Calcutta]], India in 1969, 1972 and 1974, respectively and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] Degree from [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]] in 1980.<ref name=inae1/> He did his post-doc work during 1981-1982 from [[Queen's University Belfast|Queen's University]], U.K, through [[Leverhulme Trust|Leverhulme Overseas Fellowship]].

He also worked as a visiting faculty at Tech University, Hannover during 1986-87 as well as at GSF Institute of Radiation Protection (now Leibnitz Institute), Munich in 1990 and 1992.

==Awards and recognition==
Chaudhuri has been elected as a Life Fellow of [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] "for contributions to pattern recognition, especially Indian language script OCR, document processing and natural language processing".<ref name=ieee2/><ref name=ieee1>{{cite web|title=IEEE Fellows in IEEE Region 10 Kolkata Section|publisher=IEEE|url=http://ewh.ieee.org/r10/calcutta/ieee_fellows.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140925061145/http://ewh.ieee.org/r10/calcutta/ieee_fellows.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 September 2014|accessdate=20 November 2018}}</ref> He has become a Fellow of [[IAPR|International Association for Pattern Recognition]] (IAPR) "for contributions to character recognition and speech synthesis in Indian language".<ref name=iapr1>{{cite web|title=IAPR Fellows|url=http://www.iapr.org/fellowsandawards/?ar=2#1998|publisher=IAPR|accessdate=20 November 2018}}</ref> He is also Fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS),<ref name=twas1>{{cite web|title=TWAS Fellow|url=http://twas.org/member/chaudhuri-bidyut-baran|publisher=TWAS|accessdate=20 November 2018|archive-date=19 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819191903/https://twas.org/member/chaudhuri-bidyut-baran|url-status=dead}}</ref>
[[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA),<ref>{{cite web|title=INSA Fellow|url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P07-1431|publisher=INSA|accessdate=20 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304121316/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P07-1431|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Indian National Academy of Engineering]] (INAE),<ref name="inae1"/> [[The National Academy of Sciences, India|National Academy of Sciences]] (NASI),<ref>{{cite web|publisher=NASI|title=NASI Fellows|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=C|accessdate=20 January 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315111634/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=C|archivedate=15 March 2016}}</ref> and [[IETE|Institute of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering]] (IETE). In 2011, Chaudhuri received the [[Om Prakash Bhasin Award]] for his contribution in the field of electronics and information technology.

Chaudhuri's interview on some of his works has been reported in Indian newspaper as well.<ref>{{cite news|author=The Telegraph|title= The Telegraph, India, Jan 29, 2004|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/west-bengal/a-script-on-his-keyboard/cid/1260303|accessdate=20 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|agency=TNN|author=Jayanta Gupta|work=[[The Times of India]]|date=21 August 2013|title=Now, software to decode Tagore's handwriting|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kolkata/Now-software-to-decode-Tagores-handwriting/articleshow/21946189.cms|accessdate=20 November 2018}}</ref>

He is within world's top 2% scientists and top-10 Indian [[Artificial intelligence|AI]] scientists according to a study conducted by [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{cite news|author=Smita Sinha|title=Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators. PLoS Biol 18(10): e3000918, 2020.|doi=10.1371/journal.pbio.3000918 |doi-access=free }}</ref> 
He has also been featured as top-10 machine learning researcher from India.<ref>{{cite news|author=Smita Sinha|date=6 September 2020|work=Analytics India Magazine |title=Top 10 Machine Learning Researchers In India|url= https://analyticsindiamag.com/top-10-machine-learning-researchers-in-india/}}</ref>
